query: Which material can be used for Temperature-dependent plastic deformation behaviors, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy (HEA) exhibits distinct temperature‐dependent plastic deformation behaviors, where the dominant deformation mechanism transitions from slip and twinning at lower temperatures to dynamic recovery and partial recrystallization at higher temperatures.
generation.material_initial_state: SLM-built equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA with a single-phase face-centered cubic (FCC) structure, fine grains, and high dislocation density.
generation.intervention: Systematic variation of the testing temperature from sub-ambient/cryogenic levels up to elevated temperatures (e.g., 25 °C to 800 °C) using standard mechanical testing (tensile/compression tests) combined with microstructural characterization.
generation.conditions: Controlled mechanical tests conducted in a broad temperature range while tracking changes in yield strength, ductility, and microstructural features (such as twin formation, dislocation density, and signs of recrystallization).
generation.structural_mediator: Temperature-induced changes in stacking fault energy and consequent microstructural evolution (e.g., formation and evolution of deformation twins, dislocation networks, and initiation of recrystallized regions).
generation.mechanism: At lower temperatures, limited thermal activation favors dislocation slip and twinning as the main deformation modes, while at higher temperatures increased atomic mobility facilitates partial recrystallization and dynamic recovery, leading to altered stress–strain behavior.
generation.predicted_outcome: A measurable shift in the mechanical performance of the alloy: a high yield strength and limited ductility at low temperatures primarily due to slip and twinning, transitioning to reduced yield strength with increased ductility at elevated temperatures due to dynamic recovery and recrystallization mechanisms.
generation.baseline: Performance metrics (yield strength, ductility, and microstructural state) measured at room temperature.
generation.boundary: Findings are based on SLM-fabricated equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA under controlled processing conditions; behavior in HEAs with other compositions or different processing routes may differ.
generation.uncertainty: The precise transition temperature and the quantitative extent of the changes in mechanical properties depend on the processing history and testing environment. Further experimental data is needed to define these parameters more exactly.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare a series of SLM-built equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA samples and perform tensile and creep experiments over a temperature range from 25 °C to 800 °C. Use real-time microstructural characterization methods (TEM, EBSD) to track the onset and evolution of slip, twinning, and recrystallization features.
measurements: Yield strength and ductility at each test temperature
Quantitative analysis of microstructural features such as dislocation density, twin formation, and recrystallized grain fraction
Stress–strain curves to capture transition behavior
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If no significant variation in deformation mechanisms or mechanical performance (e.g., no observable transition from slip/twinning to recrystallization/dynamic recovery) is detected across the tested temperature range, the hypothesis will be falsified.

Recent studies have shown attractive mechanical properties of HEAs at cryogenic temperature [4] and room temperature [5] with excellent combinations of high strength and toughness, indicating their potential as the structural materials. However, the strength of single phase type HEAs were reported to be insufficient at elevated temperatures [6] . Abstract The microstructure, temperature-dependent mechanical properties and deformation behaviors of equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy (HEA) additively manufactured by selective laser melting (SLM) were investigated. SLM-built HEA had a face-centered cubic (FCC) single-phase random solid solution. In addition, SLM-built HEA was composed of epitaxial growth grains, dislocation network and nano-sized oxides. Room- and high-temperature compression tests confirmed that SLM-built HEA has outstanding mechanical properties in all temperature ranges compared to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEAs reported up to the present. The excellent mechanical properties of SLM-built HEA were achieved with fine grains, high dislocation density and fine precipitates at low temperatures (25 °C to 600 °C), and by high dislocation density and fine precipitates at high temperatures (700 °C or higher). On the other hand, the deformation microstructure showed that slip and deformation twins are the main deformation mechanisms from 25 °C to 600 °C, and slip and partial recrystallization are the main deformation mechanisms above 700 °C. Unlike other conventional alloys based on a “principal element,” high-entropy alloy (HEA) is a unique material that maintains a random solid solution structure without forming intermetallic compounds in operating temperatures due to its high configurational entropy [1] – [3] . It also has outstanding physical and chemical properties, which makes it a potential replacement for traditional metallic materials, and it has recently been referred to as a multi-principal element alloy (MPEA) or compositionally concentrated alloy (CCA) [4] – [9] .

As attention in HEAs increases, many studies have been conducted to explore its mechanical, physical and chemical properties [10] – [15] . In particular, equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA, which was the first developed HEA, is the most studied because of its excellent combination of tensile strength and elongation along with excellent fracture toughness and corrosion resistance [6] , [16] – [21] . However, despite the advantages of equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA, many issues arise owing to its low yield strength and costly and complex thermomechanical processing (i.e., multiple casting → hot rolling → homogenization → cold rolling → annealing → cutting, etc.
